content.title: About
content.content: Cuban bread is a traditional white loaf made from wheat flour, yeast, water, and salt. After baking it is often toasted until golden and crisp, creating a fragrant, crunchy product that is served for breakfast, in sandwiches, or as a side to soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cuban bread is known for its soft interior and slightly sweet flavor thanks to a small amount of sugar in the dough.
It is traditionally baked in long loaves that are later sliced and toasted.
In Cuba the bread is commonly served with butter, cheese, ham, or avocado, creating the popular "Cubano" sandwich.
Toasting enhances caramelization, giving the crust a crunch while the crumb stays tender.
Some regions add a little milk to the dough, resulting in an even softer texture.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The bread provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fermentation by yeast produces B1, B2, and B3 vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Although not whole‑grain, Cuban bread still contains a modest amount of fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, which are essential for blood and bone health.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Toasted Cuban bread pairs well with proteins and vegetables, helping to create a balanced meal.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The bread contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White bread can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, which may be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Traditional recipes may contain a fair amount of salt; those monitoring sodium should limit portions.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to wheat flour.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted Cuban bread is used as a base for sandwiches, as a side to soups, or simply with butter and cheese. It can be cubed for salads, made into croutons, or served with avocado and tomatoes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage, freeze slices and toast them before eating.
